messages:
maya: quick check — trying to finish onboarding for zeta-13b-v2. I kicked off the HF->S3 mirror but the registry shows 403 for the target path and the tokenizer smoke failed on a sample prompt. anyone on perms or manifest?

sam: I can look. which s3 path are you hitting?

maya: s3://redwood-artifacts/zeta-13b/v2/ — the mirror job logs show presign ok but head-object returns 403 for the bucket/key. also our tokenizer test produced an extra PAD token at the start for a few sequences.

leo: I saw a similar pad/offset quirk last month with the hf tokenizer variant that included legacy pad token id=0 even when model expects =1. are you using the tokenizer from the HF repo or our normalized tokenizer?

maya: HF repo, tag v2.0. We saw pad id=0 in small sample. I tried switching to our normalizer and it fixed the pad but then the checksum on shard-0003 didn't match after mirror.

sam: assigning myself to s3 perms. quickly checking ACLs and bucket policy. @artifact-bot can you post the mirror job id and the manifest hash?

artifact-bot: mirror-job: 2026-03-16-0241, manifest_sha256: a3f9c2d4b1f6e8c0d2f4f3e0b7c1234a6d7e8f9b0c1d2e3f4b5c6d7e8f9a0b1

sam: thanks — running a head-object now:
```
aws s3api head-object --bucket redwood-artifacts --key zeta-13b/v2/shard-0003.bin
# -> An error occurred (403) when calling the HeadObject operation: Forbidden
```

ryan: re: checksum, can you paste the local md5 for shard-0003? our mirror computes md5 and stores as metadata x-amz-meta-md5. sometimes multipart uploads use etag != md5.

maya: local md5: 9f2c4a1b0d3e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4c, remote metadata etag: "d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e-3" — looks like multipart etag.

leo: yup multipart. we need to use the stored x-amz-meta-md5 value instead of ETag. that explains mismatch. can we re-run mirror with single-part for this shard? it's small (~12MB) so it should be single part. why did it go multipart?

sam: bucket policy has enforce-sse + block-public access, but nothing that should force multipart. checking the upload client settings. maya, which mirror worker image did you use?

maya: worker v3.2.1, started by the HF-handoff pipeline. PR is open with the config change: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-registry/pull/472 (pinging code-review owners @leo).

leo: on it — will review config PR today. quick note: if we switch tokenizer to normalized one, add an eval step in CI so pad/id regressions are caught.

ryan: for immediate unblock: sam, can you temporarily add maya's service account to the bucket ACL so she can fetch the shards and re-upload single-part? then we can re-run the mirror job.

sam: I can add a short-lived grant. adding now — presign should succeed after ACL update, confirm?

maya: verifying... head-object now returns 200, thanks! re-downloading shard-0003 and re-uploading single part. will post updated manifest_sha256 when done.

artifact-bot: manifest update: mirror-job: 2026-03-16-0241-retry, manifest_sha256: b7d9c3e5a0f1b2c3d4e5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f9a0b1c2d3e4f5a6b7c8d9e0

leo: great. after you reupload, can you also run the tokenizer smoke with our normalized tokenizer and attach the example that previously exhibited PAD=0? small test snippet is fine.

maya: will do. my followup checklist: (1) reupload single-part shards, (2) update manifest + presign TTL comment in PR, (3) switch tokenizer in onboarding job to normalized + add CI eval, (4) ping @eng-oncall if perf/regressions show up.

ryan: sounds good. thanks for handling the ACL dance — lesson: mirror job should assert single-part for <100MB shards and fail loudly if multipart etag detected. file an infra issue?

maya: filing infra issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/issues/981 — title: "mirror: enforce single-part uploads for small shards / surface multipart etag"

sam: done reviewing ACLs, reverted the temporary grant for safety. if you need longer access open a ticket.

maya: noted. wrapping up now — will comment back here once CI pass and PR merges. :thumbsup:
